questions.q: In a democracy, where does the ultimate source of power and authority lie?
options: With the citizens of the country
questions.explanation: Democracy is a form of government in which the source of power and authority lies with the citizens, who elect their representatives through free and fair elections.
questions.fact: Democracy is a form of government in which the source of power and authority lies with the citizens of the country.

questions.q: When did the Constitution of India come into force?
questions.explanation: The Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949 but came into force only on 26 January 1950, the day celebrated as Republic Day.
questions.fact: The Constitution of India was adopted on 26 November 1949 and came into force on 26 January 1950.

questions.q: Which of these were assemblies of the Vedic period that involved collective decision-making?
questions.explanation: The Sabha, Samiti and Vidhata were assemblies of the Vedic period that practised collective decision-making, showing democracy's early roots in India.
questions.fact: Assemblies of the Vedic period such as Sabha, Samiti, and Vidhata involved collective decision-making.

questions.q: The verse from the Aikyamatya Suktam of the Rig Veda emphasises the importance of:
options: Collective thinking, shared discussion and unity of purpose
questions.explanation: The verse values collective thinking, shared discussion and unity of purpose, showing that consultation, consensus and shared responsibility have deep roots in India's intellectual and cultural traditions.
questions.fact: A verse from the Aikyamatya Suktam of the Rig Veda emphasises the importance of collective thinking, shared discussion, and unity of purpose.

questions.q: In which year was the Constituent Assembly formed to draft India's Constitution?
questions.explanation: The Constituent Assembly was formed in 1946, before India attained independence in 1947, to draft a constitution for the country.
questions.fact: Before India attained independence in 1947, the Constituent Assembly was formed in 1946 to draft a constitution for the country.

questions.q: How long did the Constituent Assembly take to draft the Constitution?
questions.explanation: It took the Constituent Assembly 2 years, 11 months and 18 days to draft the world's longest written Constitution.
questions.fact: It took the Assembly 2 years, 11 months, and 18 days to draft the world's longest written Constitution.

questions.q: According to the chapter, what is the real strength of a democracy?
options: Its citizens—their participation, awareness of rights and duties, and commitment to honesty and fairness
questions.explanation: The real strength of democracy lies in its citizens—their participation, awareness of duties and rights, and commitment to honesty and fairness; without these, no democratic institution can function effectively.
questions.fact: The real strength of democracy lies in its citizens—their participation, awareness of duties and rights, and commitment to honesty and fairness.

questions.q: Every citizen aged 18 years and above has the right to vote through a secret ballot. What is this right called?
questions.explanation: The right of every citizen aged 18 years and above to vote through a secret ballot is known as Universal Adult Franchise.
questions.fact: Every citizen, 18 years of age and above, has the right to vote through a secret ballot. This right is known as the Universal Adult Franchise.

questions.q: India is the world's largest democracy, with a voter base of over 96.8 crore (in 2024).
questions.explanation: With a population of over 140 crore and over 96.8 crore registered voters in 2024, India represents the largest participatory democracy in the world.
questions.fact: India is the world's largest democracy... with a population of over 140 crore and a voter base of over 96.8 crore (in 2024).

questions.q: In early India, the king was an independent ruler who never consulted assemblies or ministers.
questions.explanation: From the earliest times, the king was not an independent ruler; he worked in consultation with assemblies, ministers and officers of various capacities.
questions.fact: The king was not an independent ruler but rather worked in consultation with assemblies, ministers and officers of various capacities.

questions.q: The Constituent Assembly's Debates reflect the belief that the Constitution should be a rigid legal code that never changes.
questions.explanation: The Debates reflect the members' belief that the Constitution should not be a rigid legal code but a dynamic document capable of evolving through lawful amendments without compromising its fundamental values.
questions.fact: The CAD reflects the members' belief that the constitution should not be a rigid legal code, but a dynamic document capable of evolving through lawful amendments without compromising its fundamental values.

questions.q: Only indigenous traditions shaped the Constitution; the global spread of democratic values had no influence on the Constituent Assembly's Debates.
questions.explanation: Apart from indigenous democratic traditions, the global spread of democratic values also influenced the Constituent Assembly's Debates, contributing to a robust, flexible, transformative and responsive constitution.
questions.fact: Apart from the indigenous democratic traditions, the global spread of democratic values also influenced the Constituent Assembly's Debates (CAD).

questions.q: The Constitution of India was adopted on 26 November ___ and came into force on 26 January 1950.
questions.explanation: The Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949 and came into force on 26 January 1950, which is celebrated as Republic Day.
questions.fact: The Constitution of India was adopted on 26 November 1949 and came into force on 26 January 1950.

questions.q: Owing to its critical role in safeguarding people's voices, the media is often referred to as the '___ pillar of democracy'.
questions.explanation: Media is called the fourth pillar of democracy because it keeps people informed, raises public issues and serves as a voice of the masses.
questions.fact: Owing to its critical role in safeguarding people's voices and upholding democratic principles, media is often referred to as the 'fourth pillar of democracy'.

questions.q: In the chapter, 'India, that is, ___', represents the largest participatory democracy in the world.
questions.explanation: The chapter uses the phrase 'India, that is, Bharat' while describing the largest participatory democracy, where people choose their government by electing their representatives.
questions.fact: India, that is, Bharat, represents the largest participatory democracy, where people choose their government by electing their representatives.
questions.hint: The chapter uses India's ancient Sanskrit name.

questions.q: Match each leader with what the chapter associates them with.

pairs.r: Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constitution
Founded the Bauddha Sangha, where members chose their leader through voting
Led the government when the Emergency was imposed
Advocated for the rights of the rural poor

questions.explanation: Each leader is linked to a specific contribution—Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee, Buddha founded the voting Sangha, Narayan was the Lok Nayak, the Emergency came during Indira Gandhi's government, and Charan Singh championed the rural poor.
questions.fact: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar was Chairman of the Drafting Committee; the Bauddha Sangha was established by Gautama Buddha; Jayaprakash Narayan was popularly known as Lok Nayak; the Emergency was imposed during the government led by Indira Gandhi; Charan Singh advocated for the rights of the rural poor.

questions.q: Arrange the stages in the evolution of democratic ideas in India in the correct order.
orderItems: Assemblies like the Sabha and Samiti practised collective decision-making
The Bauddha Sangha chose its leaders through voting
British rule limited people's participation in governance
The independence struggle revived and strengthened democratic ideas
The Constituent Assembly drafted the Constitution
questions.explanation: India's democratic ethos evolved from Vedic assemblies and the Bauddha Sangha, was disrupted by British colonial rule, revived by the freedom struggle, and finally took constitutional form in the Constituent Assembly.
questions.fact: The democratic ethos in India did not emerge suddenly; rather, it evolved through a long historical process.

questions.q: Select all rights that are among the six Fundamental Rights in the Indian Constitution.
questions.explanation: The six Fundamental Rights are the Right to Equality, Right to Freedom, Right Against Exploitation, Right to Freedom of Religion, Cultural and Educational Rights, and the Right to Constitutional Remedies; the Right to Property is not among them.
questions.fact: There are six Fundamental Rights—the Right to Equality (Articles 14-18); the Right to Freedom (Articles 19-22); the Right Against Exploitation (Articles 23-24); the Right to Freedom of Religion (Articles 25-28); Cultural and Educational Rights (Articles 29-30); and the Right to Constitutional Remedies (Article 32).

questions.q: Select all correct challenges that Indian democracy continues to face, according to the chapter.
options: Spread of fake news through social media
questions.explanation: The chapter lists illiteracy, misinformation such as fake news, inequality, poverty, regionalism, gender inequality and social discrimination as challenges; Universal Adult Franchise is a democratic strength, not a challenge.
questions.fact: India continues to face several challenges, such as illiteracy, misinformation, and inequality... poverty, regionalism, gender inequality, and social discrimination also create barriers to equal participation.

questions.q: Which of these statements about democracy is INCORRECT?
options: In a democracy, the source of power and authority lies with the citizens.
In a democracy, only educated citizens have the right to participate in decision-making.
Democracy is founded on the principles of freedom, equality, justice, rights and duties.
In a democracy, citizens elect their representatives through free and fair elections.
questions.explanation: Democracy guarantees every citizen the right to vote, express opinions and participate in decision-making—education is never a condition for participation.
questions.fact: Democracy is founded on the principles of freedom, equality, justice, rights and duties, ensuring that citizens have the right to vote, express their opinions, and participate in the decision-making processes.

questions.q: Which of these statements about the Constitution is INCORRECT?
options: The Constitution of India was adopted on 26 November 1949 and came into force on 26 January 1950.
The Constitution guarantees and protects the Fundamental Rights of all citizens.
The Constitution permits discrimination on the basis of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth.
The Constitution encourages active citizen participation at the national, state and local levels through elections.
questions.explanation: The Constitution ensures that no citizen is discriminated against on the basis of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth.
questions.fact: It ensures that no citizen is discriminated against on the basis of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth.

questions.q: Which of these statements about types of democracy is INCORRECT?
options: Direct democracy is easy to practise in large countries like India.
In a direct democracy, citizens directly participate in most decision-making processes.
In a representative democracy, people elect their representatives and do not directly govern.
A representative democracy holds periodic elections and the government is accountable to the people.
questions.explanation: Direct democracy is difficult to follow in large countries, which is why large democracies like India practise representative democracy instead.
questions.fact: Direct Democracy: Citizens directly participate in most decision-making processes... Difficult to follow in large countries. e.g. Switzerland.
questions.hint: Think about how practical it is for over 140 crore people to vote on every single decision.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The media is often referred to as the 'fourth pillar of democracy'.
Reason (R): Media plays a critical role in safeguarding people's voices and upholding democratic principles.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, and the media's role in safeguarding people's voices and upholding democratic principles is exactly why it earns the title of the fourth pillar of democracy.
questions.fact: Owing to its critical role in safeguarding people's voices and upholding democratic principles, media is often referred to as the 'fourth pillar of democracy'.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): In a parliamentary democracy, the people directly elect the executive.
Reason (R): In a parliamentary democracy, members of the executive are also part of the legislature.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.explanation: In a parliamentary democracy, people elect the legislature but not the executive; since members of the executive come from the legislature, A is false while R is true.
questions.fact: Parliamentary Democracy: Members of the Executive are also part of the legislature... People elect the legislature but not the executive.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): A constitution plays a crucial role in safeguarding the rights of the people in a democracy.
Reason (R): The Constitution of India not only guarantees but also protects the Fundamental Rights of all citizens.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, and the Constitution's guarantee and protection of Fundamental Rights illustrates exactly how a constitution safeguards people's rights in a democracy.
questions.fact: A constitution plays a crucial role in safeguarding the rights of the people in a democracy... The Constitution not only guarantees but also protects the Fundamental Rights of all citizens.
